items.title: Spotify vs. Netflix: I’d Bet on This Streaming Stock for the Next 5 Years
items.summary: Spotify and Netflix just reported quarters that point in completely different directions, and the gap between their strategies raises a question worth sitting with: which business actually has more room to run from here?

items.title: How Far Could Alphabet Stock Move On You In A Year?
items.summary: Alphabet (GOOGL) stock trades at about $332, and options expiring roughly a year out price a 68% probability range running from roughly $233 to roughly $474. That floor sits just under the stock's 52-week low of $235.96, while the ceiling clears its 52-week high of $402.12. Yet, a range this wide is close to normal for these shares, not a sign of unusual fear.

items.title: Netflix Said It Was Different From Facebook. A New Lawsuit Says It Tracked Kids for Ads Anyway.
items.summary: Florida is suing Netflix for billions, accusing the streaming giant of secretly tracking children for advertisers while publicly promising families a safe alternative to social media surveillance. The outcome could unravel the economics powering Netflix's fastest-growing business.

items.title: Is The AI Capex Surge A Threat To Amazon Stock?
items.summary: Amazon.com (AMZN) plans to spend roughly $220 billion of cash on capital in 2026, against $775.7 billion of revenue over the trailing twelve months. The sheer size of that bill introduces notable capital allocation and cash flow pressures that investors must weigh. The rest is who sets the number, and how long the money has to stay out before any of it comes back.
